parts.visual:
You pour 100 liters of water into a bucket every minute. But the bucket has a massive hole at the bottom, leaking 90 liters a minute. To fill the bucket, you have to spend millions on more water.

The Math:
1. Churn Rate: The percentage of customers who cancel their subscription or stop using the product within a given time period.
2. Retention Rate: The percentage of customers who stay.
3. The Reality: High churn means your product is a 'Vitamin'. If you don't fix the leak, you will run out of money trying to buy new users.
parts.audio: Investors do not care how many new users you acquire if your Churn Rate is high. A high churn rate proves that your product does not have Product-Market Fit. It is the ultimate diagnostic metric for the health of a startup.

questions.question: A consumer app has a monthly churn rate of 20%. This means 20% of their users cancel every single month. What will happen in 5 months?
options: Mathematically, they will lose 100% of their original user base. To survive, the marketing team must perform miracles every month just to replace the people leaving.
questions.correct_answer: Mathematically, they will lose 100% of their original user base. To survive, the marketing team must perform miracles every month just to replace the people leaving.
questions.explanation: Consumer apps often have high churn, which is why they are incredibly difficult to scale.

questions.question: Listen to the B2B SaaS CEO. What is her ultimate goal?
questions.tts_text: We don't just want a 0% churn rate. We want 'Negative Churn'. We want the customers who stay to upgrade their accounts and pay us so much more money that it completely covers the revenue we lose from the few people who cancel.
options: Net Negative Churn. This is the holy grail of SaaS. It means your company grows revenue automatically every month, even if your marketing team acquires exactly zero new customers.
questions.correct_answer: Net Negative Churn. This is the holy grail of SaaS. It means your company grows revenue automatically every month, even if your marketing team acquires exactly zero new customers.
questions.explanation: Negative churn happens through 'Upsells' and 'Expansion Revenue'.

questions.question: What is 'Cohort Analysis'?
options: Tracking a specific group of users (e.g., 'Everyone who signed up in January') over time to see exactly when and why they drop off. It helps pinpoint the exact moment the product fails them.
questions.correct_answer: Tracking a specific group of users (e.g., 'Everyone who signed up in January') over time to see exactly when and why they drop off. It helps pinpoint the exact moment the product fails them.
questions.explanation: If every cohort cancels on Day 14, you know exactly where to fix the software.

questions.question: Why is B2B Enterprise software fundamentally more valuable than B2C Consumer apps?
options: Because B2B Enterprise software has artificially low churn. Once a Fortune 500 company integrates your software into their operations, the 'Switching Costs' are so painful they will almost never cancel.
